title: Fan-to-Artist Economy
tagline: Web3 direct-to-fan music and NFT ticketing
description: Group 2's analysis of blockchain in the music industry — streaming, tokenized royalties and NFT concert tickets — with a managerial deep dive into NFT ticket resale that fights fake tickets and scalping while paying artists a share of secondary sales.
competitive_advantage: Compared with a traditional database run by one operator, blockchain offers shared verification across parties, a tamper-resistant transaction history and programmable, verifiable smart contracts — at the cost of extra technical complexity.

founder.name: Group 2 — Financial Decision Making & Blockchain Application
founder.position: Supervised by Dr. Pan Theo Grosse-Ruyken

overview.executiveSummary: Blockchain enables direct artist-to-fan connections via smart contracts, removing unnecessary gatekeepers and turning fans from passive consumers into active participants and co-owners. The project asks how blockchain is applied in music and what real industry problems it genuinely solves, focusing on copyright, royalties, music NFTs, fan engagement and ticketing.
overview.problemStatement: Middleman dominance: artists receive only about 12% of the $43 billion in total revenue. Opaque copyrights: ownership metadata is fragmented and unclear. Delayed royalties: payouts take 6–18 months through complex layers. In ticketing: fake tickets, scalping, uncontrolled resale, lack of identity, and artists receiving little or nothing from the resale market.
overview.proposedSolution: Public transparency through immutable on-chain ownership records, verifiable digital assets for fans, and smart contracts for instant, automated royalty distribution. For ticketing: an NFT gives verifiable ticket ownership, smart contracts set programmable resale rules, KYC verifies identity, and royalty rules let artists receive part of the resale revenue — with resale through an official marketplace and every ownership transfer recorded on-chain.
overview.expectedImpact: Easier ticket authentication and ownership verification, better control of secondary sales, and a share of resale revenue for artists — depending on real users, events, transactions and revenue

team.experience: Group 2 of the Financial Decision Making & Blockchain Application programme, supervised by Dr. Pan Theo Grosse-Ruyken (PTGR).

product.description: Real-world applications: Audius — a decentralized music streaming platform with direct artist–fan connection and 250M+ streams reported by 2025. Royal — music NFTs that tokenize royalty rights so fans can earn a share of royalties. GET Protocol — NFT ticketing with verifiable ownership and programmable resale rules. BitSong — 3,000+ users, ~2 million blocks and 300%+ team growth, addressing royalty transparency and dependence on intermediaries.
product.features: Recommended architecture: blockchain handles ownership management, ticket anti-counterfeiting and business logic via smart contracts, with duties separated between public and private chains; traditional systems handle privacy and identity management, a secondary database for real-time access authentication, and the web service and payment gateway.
product.techStack: Blockchain, Smart Contracts, NFTs, KYC, Public & Private Chains

risks.risk: Bots in the primary ticket market remain hard to prevent
User adoption barriers and crypto-wallet requirements
Legal challenges and no common framework (copyright, consumer protection, data privacy, ticketing, tax)
Long-term sustainability across technical (security, scalability, fees), operational (KYC, support, marketplace) and economic (revenue, operating cost) areas
